solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Boss to lead old lady around area

indicators.note: going around turns the word for an old lady back on itself, so it is read from right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
Pb is the chemical symbol for the metal lead
a nana is a grandmother, an old lady of the family
A is the standard abbreviation for area

explanation.surface: Someone told to escort an elderly lady around the neighbourhood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' looks like a verb meaning escort, but it is the metal, symbol Pb. TOP BANANA is the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Top banana is informal slang for the most important person in a group, the chief or person in charge.

clue.text: Lacking enthusiasm, quietly stops revolutionary eating plan

indicators.note: something revolutionary turns right over, so the following word is read backwards
to stop a hole is to plug it, so one piece is lodged inside the other like a stopper

blocks.note: p, for piano, is the musical direction meaning quietly
a diet is a plan for eating

explanation.surface: A half-hearted dieter quietly gives up on a radical new eating regime.
explanation.walkthrough: DIET is turned around to TEID, and P is plugged into the middle to give TEPID.
explanation.definitionFit: Tepid literally means lukewarm, and figuratively describes a response showing little keenness or passion.

clue.text: Re-employing dull temps in Oban, Mansfield and Harlow?

definitions.note: definition by example: two famous instances, hence the question mark

indicators.note: employing again implies putting the letters to work in a fresh arrangement

blocks.note: taken as written: every letter of these four words is rearranged

explanation.surface: An agency rehiring boring temporary staff in Oban, Mansfield and Harlow, which look like three British towns.
explanation.walkthrough: Mansfield and Harlow pose as English towns beside Oban, but they are Jayne Mansfield and Jean Harlow, Hollywood stars famous for very pale hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Jayne Mansfield and Jean Harlow were both iconic film actresses with silvery white bleached hair.

clue.text: Mantel openly defends bounder

indicators.note: to defend is to guard and enclose, so the words wrap protectively around the solution

blocks.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Novelist Hilary Mantel openly sticks up for a cad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounder' looks like old slang for a rogue, but here it is literal: an animal that bounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Antelopes are swift grazing animals famous for leaping and springing as they run, so one is a bounder.

clue.text: One acted out story

indicators.note: acted out suggests a performance, and 'out' also means disordered, so these letters get scrambled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone performed a tale for an audience.
explanation.definitionFit: An anecdote is a short amusing or interesting account of a real incident, a kind of tale.

clue.text: Too grand to follow apprentice’s lead

indicators.note: a lead is what goes in front, so only the opening letter of that word is wanted
following means coming after, so the word for grand is placed behind the other piece

blocks.note: the opening letter of apprentice
swell is an old-fashioned word for excellent or grand

explanation.surface: A trainee is too important to follow the lead of a mere apprentice.
explanation.definitionFit: As well and too are interchangeable adverbs meaning also or in addition.

clue.text: Bathroom fixture picked up two days before D-Day?

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, as a radio picks up a signal, so we go by sound

blocks.note: if D-Day is day D, the day before is C-Day and the day before that is B-Day

explanation.surface: A plumbing fitting collected shortly before the Normandy landings.
explanation.walkthrough: Count back through the alphabet from D-Day: two letters back is B, so B-Day, which is said just like the French-derived bidet.
explanation.definitionFit: A bidet is a low basin used for washing, installed beside the toilet in many bathrooms.

clue.text: Two types of neckwear for keen rower

blocks.note: first type: a boa is a long feathery scarf
second type: a tie is worn knotted at the collar

explanation.surface: Recommended neckwear for a rowing enthusiast.
explanation.definitionFit: Boatie is an informal word, chiefly Australian and New Zealand, for someone devoted to rowing or boating.

clue.text: Modifying word in clear piece of writing

blocks.note: definite means clear and certain
an article is a piece written for a newspaper or magazine

explanation.surface: An editor spots a qualifying word in a lucid essay.
explanation.walkthrough: The definite article is the grammatical name for the word 'the'.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar 'the' is a determiner that qualifies a noun, so it is a word that modifies another.

clue.text: Material heartless old jailer read aloud

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter is cut out of the word for a jailer
saying something aloud means we want how the word sounds, not how it is spelt

blocks.note: a turnkey was a prison warder who kept the keys
in the past tense, read is pronounced exactly like the colour

explanation.surface: A cruel old prison guard reads out the charges against an inmate.
explanation.walkthrough: TURNKEY loses its middle letter N to give TURKEY, then RED sounds like the past tense of read.
explanation.definitionFit: Turkey red is a bright scarlet dyed cotton cloth, once widely produced, so it is a type of fabric.

clue.text: Predators initially unnerve rabbit

indicators.note: initially means at the beginning, so only the opening letter of the preceding word counts

blocks.note: the opening letter of predators
to rattle someone is to unsettle them

explanation.surface: Hunting animals first make a bunny jumpy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rabbit' looks like the prey animal, but here it is British slang for chatter, as in rabbit on.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to rabbit is to talk at length about trivia, which is to chatter or babble.

clue.text: Hiding? How come?

blocks.note: first meaning: a beating or severe telling-off, as in to give someone a hiding
second meaning: a question asking for the reason, meaning why

explanation.walkthrough: 'Hiding' looks like concealment, but it is the British sense of a thrashing; to give someone what for is to punish them.
explanation.definitionFit: To give someone what for is an idiom for punishing or scolding them, and the phrase also asks why.

clue.text: Train people to shun baboon

indicators.note: shunning means keeping away, so these letters stay out of the animal's name

blocks.note: to man a ship is to people it, to staff it with crew
the mandrill is a large brightly faced baboon

explanation.surface: Teaching a group of humans to keep clear of a large monkey.
explanation.walkthrough: MANDRILL minus MAN leaves DRILL, which is also another kind of baboon, a nice touch.
explanation.definitionFit: To drill soldiers or pupils is to instruct them by repeated practice exercises.

clue.text: Marriage following conclusion of dogged flirtation

indicators.note: a conclusion is the end, so only the final letter of that word is taken
following means coming after, so the word for marriage sits behind the other piece

blocks.note: the final letter of dogged
a marriage is an alliance between two people or families

explanation.surface: A wedding comes after a persistent spell of flirting.
explanation.definitionFit: A dalliance is a casual romantic involvement or the act of amorous trifling, much like flirting.

clue.text: Chartered surveyor consuming alcohol and favourite cakes

indicators.note: consuming means taking in, so the surveyor's letters swallow the drink and the pet

blocks.note: CS is the abbreviation for chartered surveyor
rum is an alcoholic spirit
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A surveyor enjoys a drink and their favourite pastries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Favourite' looks like an adjective for the cakes, but it is a noun of its own; a chartered surveyor is a qualified UK property professional.
explanation.definitionFit: Crumpets are soft griddle-baked rounds eaten toasted with butter, a kind of small teatime bread cake.

clue.text: Natural consequence of putting Toyota on railway

indicators.note: putting one thing on another stacks them, so in this down clue the car comes first above the railway

blocks.note: the Corolla is a popular Toyota car model
RY is an abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: What happens when you load a Toyota car onto a train line.
explanation.definitionFit: A corollary is a proposition or result that follows directly and inevitably from something already established.

clue.text: Regularly use satnav, driver’s ultimate navigational aid

indicators.note: using something regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the device is kept
ultimate means the last one, so only the final letter of that word is wanted

blocks.note: the first, third and fifth letters of satnav
the final letter of driver

explanation.surface: A motorist relying on satellite navigation as their key guide.
explanation.walkthrough: Before satnav, sailors steered by the stars, so the whole clue reads both ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Navigators have long fixed their position at sea by sighting a fixed heavenly body such as the Pole Star.

clue.text: George avoids seafood

blocks.note: Geo. is the old abbreviation for the name George
to duck something is to dodge or avoid it

explanation.surface: A man named George steers clear of fish dishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Avoids' looks like a linking verb, but it supplies letters of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: The geoduck is a giant burrowing clam from the Pacific coast of North America, eaten as a delicacy.

clue.text: Brief excitement over ancient statesman bowing in a certain way

indicators.note: something brief is cut short, so the word for excitement loses its last letter
in a down clue being over something means sitting above it, so this piece comes first

blocks.note: spice is zest or excitement, as in variety is the spice of life
Cato was a Roman statesman famous for severity

explanation.surface: A thrill to see a classical politician bowing in a particular manner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bowing' suggests leaning forward politely, but it is how a violinist moves the bow. SPICE shortened to SPIC goes above CATO.
explanation.definitionFit: Spiccato is a string-playing technique where the bow bounces lightly off the strings for detached notes.

clue.text: Fortieth head of government to come out of public school

indicators.note: the head of something is its top, so only the opening letter of that word is used
coming out of a place means leaving it, so that letter is removed from the school

blocks.note: the opening letter of government
Rugby is a famous English public school, which in Britain means a fee-paying private school

explanation.surface: Forty years on, a prime minister emerges from an elite private school.
explanation.walkthrough: RUGBY loses its G to leave RUBY. Ruby is the traditional gift for a fortieth wedding anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: Anniversaries are named after traditional gifts, and the fortieth wedding anniversary is the ruby one.

clue.text: I pleaded slyly and plotted secretly

indicators.note: acting slyly means being crafty and twisting things, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A conspirator confesses to cunning pleading and covert scheming.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep-laid describes schemes that are carefully and covertly devised well in advance.

clue.text: Female setter’s Greek god

blocks.note: her is the female pronoun
the setter refers to themselves as me, so setter's is me's

explanation.surface: A woman compiler's crossword features a deity from Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords the setter is me, so setter's gives ME'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermes was the Olympian messenger deity with winged sandals in ancient mythology.

clue.text: Part of shower cap worn by heroine, oddly absent

indicators.note: with the odd-numbered letters missing, only the second, fourth and sixth survive
something worn by another is put on and surrounds it, so the cap goes around

blocks.note: a lid is a cap or cover
the even letters of heroine

explanation.surface: A heroine wearing a shower cap in the bathroom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shower' looks like the bathroom kind, and 'cap' fits that picture, but it is a meteor shower.
explanation.definitionFit: The Leonids are an annual November meteor shower, so a Leonid is one meteor within it.

clue.text: Toilets occupied by Sale’s wingers and prop

indicators.note: wingers play on the flanks, so only the two outside letters of the word are used
a room occupied by someone has them inside it, so the letters go within

blocks.note: two toilets: a loo, and a head, which is a ship's toilet
the outside letters of Sale

explanation.surface: The changing-room toilets are taken over by the wing players of Sale, an English rugby club, and a forward.
explanation.walkthrough: A head is the sailors' word for a toilet on board ship. In rugby the loosehead prop packs down on the left of the scrum's front row.
explanation.definitionFit: Loosehead is one of the two rugby front-row forward positions, the one on the left side of the scrum.

clue.text: See you texting mate with reprimand

blocks.note: CU is text-message shorthand for see you
a ram is said to tup a ewe when it mates with her

explanation.surface: A friend signs off a text message with a telling-off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mate' looks like a pal, but it is the verb for animals breeding.
explanation.definitionFit: To cut someone up can mean to criticise or censure them harshly, an informal sense of scolding.

clue.text: Jolly camp plaintiff?

blocks.note: first meaning: a festive get-together
second meaning: a faction or side in a dispute
third meaning: one of the sides in a lawsuit

explanation.walkthrough: This is in fact a triple definition, with the question mark signalling that a plaintiff is one example of the legal sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a celebration, a group sharing a political position, and a litigant in court.

clue.text: Terribly bad sign for corporation?

definitions.note: a joking definition: corporation is old slang for a large paunch

indicators.note: something done terribly is botched, so the word that follows gets jumbled

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an omen is a portent or sign

explanation.surface: An ominous portent for a big company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' looks like a business, but it is a dated jokey word for a potbelly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation was humorous slang for a large belly, and the belly is the abdomen.

clue.text: Poet with name for posh opportunist

indicators.note: putting one thing for another means swapping it in, so the abbreviation replaces a letter

blocks.note: Geoffrey Chaucer wrote The Canterbury Tales
N is the abbreviation for name
U means upper-class, as in U and non-U language

explanation.surface: A poet trying to look upper-class to get ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: In CHAUCER the U is replaced by N to make CHANCER. U for posh comes from the 1950s U and non-U distinction in British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A chancer is a British informal term for someone who takes risks and exploits any chance for gain.

clue.text: Affirmations of my fine morals are vacuous at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of each word in the run before it

blocks.note: the final letters of the five words

explanation.surface: Someone admits that their own lofty ethical statements turn out to be empty.
explanation.definitionFit: Each yes is an affirmative reply, so several of them are statements of agreement.

clue.text: Finding divorces surprisingly variable

indicators.note: a surprising result is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknown variables

explanation.surface: A research finding that divorce rates fluctuate unexpectedly.
explanation.definitionFit: A discovery is something found or unearthed, as a finding is the result of an investigation.
